name: Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America System / Amarillo Expansion Project

values.EndLocation: New delivery point, Deaf Smith County

values.RouteNotes: Compression and a new delivery point on the existing Amarillo Line. No new pipe is described in the filing coverage.

researcher_notes: A natural gas pipeline company filed with the federal energy regulator on September 17, 2026 (docket CP26-581) to rebuild Compressor Station 112 in Moore County, Texas, and add a delivery point in Deaf Smith County. Trade press coverage of the filing lists compression, cooling equipment and station piping only. No new pipe is described, so length is staged as 0 and the row is a capacity expansion only. The new compression adds 321,200 Dth/d on the southbound Amarillo Line. With 228,800 Dth/d of existing unused space the service is 550,000 Dth/d, and the shipper has a 10-year agreement for all of it. Capacity is staged as the new 321,200 Dth/d. Data center tie: a gas trade publication names the shipper, IP Roman III Gas, an affiliate of Intersect Power (owned by Google), and links the gas to the Roman Energy Center for a Google data center campus in Hereford, Deaf Smith County. A second trade article says the gas would serve a planned data center in Deaf Smith County. The filing does not name the end user. Cost: the filing estimate is $139 million (two news reports). The operator's project page says about $200 million, with Kinder Morgan's share about $75 million. The two were not reconciled, so the filing figure is staged. Expected in service September 2028, or the third quarter per the operator. Parent system is P0222. No existing row matches this project. The Texas-Louisiana Expansion Project (P7832) is a different project. Owner is the pipeline company, which the ownership style check leaves unchanged. Source tier is medium to high: the operator page and three news articles agree on the facts, but the filing itself was not read.
